notes: Extracted 31 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/radio.guide.tsx, self-contained) and docs/evidence/radio.md at 4e470cf, the 2 October commit that adopted Biscuit's main at 3795b4c and moved the guide's Sources date to “1 October 2026” (its only change to this guide). 4e470cf is on origin/main, and origin/main and origin/docs-next have the same radio guide and evidence. The guide's Sources note and the evidence's “0.1.78 check” were checked on 1 October 2026 on 0.1.78 (mirror v0.1.78, built from 5b6894b, the #175 fix), so items citing them carry 2026-10-01 and 0.1.78-5b6894b (same package version as installed, so the trace check does not flag them). The evidence's other sections (Checked, Sources, Contract, Rendered, Limits, Verification) are the 29 September check on 0.1.77; nothing here cites them, since Radio.tsx changed between v0.1.77 (42d5bb5) and v0.1.78 (60d0658) and several of their sentences are out of date (no role, name or checked state, Space doesn't select, the focused border stays #22004a, #175 “To do”). Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). Radio.tsx is the same blob (60d0658) at v0.1.78, v0.1.78-3795b4c, v0.1.78-dbe0e02 and in node_modules, and so is RadioButton.tsx (f73c312, a re-export of Radio). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (9 commits) is cut off at 300 files, so the files Radio and the examples read were compared by blob: shadow.ts, react-utils.ts, figma-variables-resolver.ts, JFSThemeProvider.tsx, figma-modes.generated.ts, ListItem.tsx, HStack.tsx and VStack.tsx are unchanged; web-platform-utils.ts changed (useKeyboardNavigation gained an optional activationKeys; its default, Enter and Space, is what it did before, and Radio passes none); Coin Variables changed, but its 37 radio/* variables are identical at both tags; Card, Button, Checkbox, CheckboxItem and HoldingsCard changed (not read for this entry beyond their own entries). Every guide and evidence sentence quoted here was read against the installed Radio.tsx, with token values through the package's own getVariableByName in lib/commonjs (Light), and the guide page was rendered on the installed build (scratch build of the docs site, headless Chrome, 1280 px): radio/width and radio/height 18 and the circle's radius half the width (lines 85–91, 184); border 1 px (171), idle white with rgb(34, 0, 74), selected rgb(93, 0, 181) with a 10 px white dot (radio/selector/size; 87, 158–162, 195–200); hover and pressed draw the hover tokens, a 4 px rgb(237, 231, 255) glow, on both (105–112, 165–178, 192); disabled rgb(235, 235, 237) with rgb(194, 196, 199), disabled selected rgb(219, 207, 255) with rgb(201, 183, 255) and a white dot, Pressable disabled so onPress isn't called (128–136, 255); accessibilityRole radio with accessibilityState checked and disabled, accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint passed through (264–267); on the web aria-checked, aria-disabled and tabIndex -1 when disabled (205–212), and the keyboard handler runs onPress on Enter and Space unless disabled (203; rendered: role radio, aria-checked, Space selects); hitSlop 13 on each side gives 44 px (54–63, 202), and a browser still measures 18 × 18 (rendered). The focused unselected border falls back to #fd5a13 because radio/focus/border/color is still not in the packaged variables (138–147; rendered rgb(253, 90, 19) with the 4 px rgb(255, 222, 0) ring). One guide sentence does not hold and is left out: the States description's “keyboard focus adds a yellow ring and an orange border.” is true of an unselected Radio only. A focused selected Radio renders as an unfocused one (rgb(93, 0, 181), border rgb(34, 0, 74), no ring), because the orange fallback is for unselected only and radio/focusSelected/boxShadow/size is not in the packaged variables, so the ring is 0 (165, 177, 192). The published Storybook (still an older build: its Radio has no radio role) draws the same. /states/5 rests on the evidence's 0.1.78 sentence for an unselected Radio; reviews/radio.json carries a human flag for the guide sentence (candidate guide fix), and the missing ring was reported to the coordinator as a candidate Component Bug. It is not in gaps: no evidence or guide sentence records it yet. Tickets, read on the board (read only): #175 (Components, Component Bug, Done 1 October, Biscuit's fix) is fixed, and the installed source confirms it (role, checked state, accessibilityLabel, Space, the 44 px hitSlop, the focus border fallback), so it is not a gap; its ask to add radio/focus/border/color to the tokens is still open in the package, but the fallback draws Figma's colour, so nothing shows. “#220” in the evidence is part of the hex #22004a (the idle border), not a ticket; board #220 is an unrelated Duet ticket. Strength: four quotes hold absolute words. “Only the circle responds to a press” (configuration) and “On its own only the circle is pressable” (sizing) are contextual: a Radio beside a plain label or on its own. “The Radio is always 18 × 18 px.” is everywhere (no prop or mode sizes it) and stays recommended, as it describes the component. “the screen must stop a second selection” is everywhere (Radio has no group; a Radio is selected only by its own selected prop) and is the one required rule, worded as the quote: never two selected at once. Round 1 of the cross-check flagged that rule's first wording, “Keep exactly one Radio selected”, as stronger than the source (the In context screen starts with none chosen), and a wiring sentence the In context quote doesn't carry; both were reworded. avoidWhen: “Use a Checkbox for yes or no” names Checkbox, so useInstead is Checkbox (the export the guide names, as Toggle's entry does); the guide's Do shows a Checkbox Item, a labelled row with a checkbox. The Sources sentence “Radio has no label or group: the screen keeps one selected value.” is not used: /configuration/0 and /configuration/1 carry the same from the Configuration description and the Do & Don'ts. RadioButton is a deprecated alias export with no entry; /configuration/7 says only what the Sources note says. Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every Radio, Text, HStack, VStack, ListItem, Card and Button) and no other modes; the Radio in a ListItem's trailing slot takes the row's modes. They write out the guide's helpers: the In context account rows (AccountRows: a Card, a VStack, three ListItems with layout Horizontal, navArrow false, title, supportText, onPress and a trailing Radio, and the Continue Button) and the Frequencies label rows (LabelRow: an HStack with alignVertical center, a Radio and a Text), with the playground's Disable Yearly on (a disabled Radio gets no onPress, as in LabelRow). selected stands for the screen's state, as the guide's useState does. Each Radio carries an accessibilityLabel with its option, as the Sources note asks (the guide's own specimens set none). Card, Button, VStack and HStack have entries; ListItem and Text have undocumented entries. Left out of examples (three at most): the anatomy and sizing specimens (the 1.5× anatomy view, the 18 × 18 and 264 × 34 marks), the States cards, the Content cards, the three Do & Don'ts and the status line (“Choose an account”, plain page copy). Not recorded: the Pressed state (drawn as hover in the source; only the 0.1.77 Contract says so), disabled's aria-disabled and tabindex on the web (only the 0.1.77 Rendered section), accessibilityHint and testID (no guide sentence), style (the building rules keep colour, border, radius and font off Coin components), Color Mode Dark (the guide shows none; building rules), the evidence's Figma token hexes and layer counts, and the Figma variant mapping beyond the Sources sentence. Consistency with related entries: Checkbox's entry agrees (“Only one answer is allowed: use a single-choice control.”, with no useInstead, written when Radio had no entry), and so does Checkbox Item's. Holdings Card's entry agrees: its top right shows a Radio by default, the screen's onPress sets selected and the Radio fills, and disabled greys it. Slider's (“Three positions read better as Radios.”) and Toggle's (“Use a pair of Radios.”) both point to Radio with useInstead, and agree with “two to five options”; Toggle's notes still say neither Checkbox nor Radio has an entry, now out of date (reported). ListItem's undocumented entry and facts agree: trailing is a Horizontal-layout slot whose children take the row's modes, and onPress makes the whole row pressable. Nothing hand-written here, and nothing in the guide, evidence or Radio source, uses the shape word the pack avoids.
